ui.app_tagline: Solid rocket motor design & internal ballistics
ui.technical_report_hint: Scaled, dimensioned drawing with editable inputs, the parts list (BOM) and downloadable files for your records.
ui.export_locked: Export is locked while a red warning is present.
ui.export_locked_why: Fix the danger-level warning, or tick “I accept the risk”.
ui.derived_value: This value is calculated, not entered.

param.propellant_id: The sugar propellant formulation. KNSB is potassium nitrate / sorbitol; changing it changes burn rate, c* and flame temperature.
param.density_factor: How close your cast grain gets to the ideal density. 0.95 is typical for hand-poured KNSB; lower it if your grains have voids.
param.c_star_efficiency: Real performance versus the theoretical value. If you have not static-fired, 0.90–0.95 is a reasonable estimate.
param.grain_type: How the propellant burns. BATES is neutral and recommended; a tube is progressive and pushes pressure up during the burn.
param.outer_diameter: Outside diameter of the propellant grain. It has to fit inside the liner, and it sets how much propellant you have.
param.core_diameter: Diameter of the central bore. A wider core lowers pressure and thrust but shortens burn time.
param.segment_length: Length of one BATES segment. Use “Make neutral” to get the length that keeps burn area constant.
param.segment_count: Number of BATES segments stacked in the case. More segments means more burn area and higher thrust.
param.segment_spacing: Small gap left between segments for the spacers/retainers. It barely affects ballistics, only the total stack length.
param.throat_diameter: The narrowest point of the nozzle. Making it smaller raises chamber pressure and thrust; too small and the case can burst.
param.expansion_ratio: Exit area divided by throat area. Use “Optimum expansion” to match sea level; too large and the flow separates.
param.divergence_half_angle: Cone angle of the diverging section. 12–15° is normal; larger angles lose thrust to divergence.
param.convergence_half_angle: Cone angle feeding into the throat. It only affects the nozzle length, not performance; 30–45° is typical.
param.nozzle_efficiency: Lump factor for friction and non-ideal flow in the nozzle. 0.95 is a common default.
param.throat_length: Length of the straight throat section. Mostly a manufacturing choice; keep it short.
param.erosion_enabled: Whether the throat is allowed to widen during the burn. Leave off unless you have measured erosion — it is never a way to “fix” over-pressure.
param.erosion_coefficient: Recession rate constant for the graphite throat. Realistic values are 0.02–0.1 mm/s; above 0.3 the model warns you.
param.erosion_exponent: Pressure sensitivity of throat erosion. 0.8 is a common value.
param.case_material: The 3D-printed (or aluminium) chamber material. Its tensile strength and layer-adhesion factor decide the factor of safety.
param.case_inner_diameter: Bore of the case tube. The liner sits inside this, then the grain inside the liner.
param.case_wall_thickness: Wall thickness of the case tube. Thicker walls raise the factor of safety but add mass.
param.case_length: Internal length of the case. Leave blank to let it be fitted to the grain stack plus the nozzle seat.
param.print_method: How the case is made. FDM layers are weak across the print direction (factor 0.5); SLS is closer to isotropic (0.9).
param.liner_material: The ablative sleeve that protects the case from the flame. KNSB burns at ~1600 K — a plastic case will not survive without one.
param.liner_thickness: Thickness of that ablative layer. It must survive the whole burn plus a margin; long burns need more.
param.bulkhead_material: Material of the forward closure disc. It carries the full pressure blow-out force.
param.bulkhead_thickness: Thickness of the forward closure. It sets how many fasteners you need to hold it in.
param.forward_gap: Empty space between the bulkhead and the grain. A few millimetres is enough for ignition volume.
param.aft_gap: Space between the grain and the nozzle entry. Keeps the last segment off the nozzle.
param.ambient_pressure: Outside air pressure where the motor fires. Sea level is 1.013 bar; lower it for high-altitude launches.
param.meop_bar: The maximum pressure your case can take. The peak (erosionless) chamber pressure must stay below this.
param.bolt_diameter: Diameter of the shear fasteners retaining the bulkhead and nozzle. Bigger bolts mean fewer of them.
param.bolt_shear_strength: Shear strength of the fastener material. ~200 MPa is a class-4.8 steel bolt.
param.dry_mass: Loaded rocket mass without the motor’s propellant. Heavier rockets fly lower.
param.body_diameter: Airframe outer diameter. It sets the frontal area used for drag.
param.drag_coefficient: Overall drag coefficient of the rocket. 0.55 is a rough default; a clean rocket is nearer 0.4.
param.target_apogee: The altitude you want to reach. The solver looks for motors that get within a band of this.
param.rail_length: Length of the launch rail or tower. A longer rail gives more speed before the rocket is unguided.
param.max_accel_g: Acceleration limit you are willing to accept, e.g. for airframe or electronics. Default 15 g.
param.launch_altitude: Elevation of the launch site above sea level. Thinner air means less drag and a higher apogee.
param.name: A label for this motor. It appears in exports and reports.
param.prefix: A short team code put before the class designation, e.g. PARS in PARS-J240.
param.designer: Your name or handle; recorded in the .eng/.rse comment and the report.

metric.total_impulse: Area under the thrust curve — the total ‘push’. It sets the motor class letter.
metric.average_thrust: Total impulse divided by burn time. Combined with the class letter it gives the designation (e.g. J240).
metric.peak_thrust: The highest instantaneous thrust during the burn.
metric.burn_time: Time from ignition to when thrust drops back to 5 % of the peak.
metric.peak_pressure: Highest chamber pressure on the erosionless curve. This is what the case must survive (MEOP).
metric.meop: The pressure limit you told the program your case can take. If peak pressure exceeds it, export is locked until you accept the risk.
metric.specific_impulse: Impulse per unit weight of propellant burned — an efficiency number, in seconds.
metric.total_mass: Loaded motor mass at ignition, including case, nozzle and bulkhead.
metric.mass_ratio: Loaded mass divided by burnt-out mass. Higher is better for the rocket.
metric.designation: NAR-style class letter plus rounded average thrust, e.g. J240.
metric.fos: Case allowable stress divided by the stress at MEOP. Below 2.0 is not considered safe.
metric.min_j: Smallest port-area / throat-area ratio during the burn. Below 2 the gas scrubs the grain and pressure gets unpredictable.
metric.lstar: Chamber free volume divided by throat area. For KNSB roughly 250–1000 mm is normal.
metric.thrust_to_weight: Average thrust divided by lift-off weight. It should comfortably exceed 1, ideally 5+ off the rail.
metric.kn: Burning surface area divided by throat area. Larger Kn means higher chamber pressure and thrust; 150–400 is typical for KNSB.
metric.motor_mass: Loaded mass of the motor alone.
metric.inert_mass: Motor mass once all the propellant is gone.
metric.total_length: Bulkhead face to nozzle exit — the value written into the .eng header.
metric.cg_initial: Centre of gravity from the forward face at ignition.
metric.cg_burnout: Centre of gravity from the forward face at burnout.

derived.web: Web = (outer Ø − core Ø) / 2. It is how far the flame front travels, so it sets the burn time.
derived.total_length: Sum of bulkhead + grain stack + gaps + nozzle. This goes into the .eng header.
derived.lstar: L* = chamber free volume / throat area.
derived.free_volume: Gas volume in the chamber = bore volume + convergent volume − remaining propellant.
derived.cg: Mass-weighted centre of the whole assembly; it moves as propellant burns.
derived.port_diameter: Diameter of the smallest flow passage through the grain at this burn position.
derived.exit_diameter: Nozzle exit Ø = throat Ø × √(expansion ratio).
derived.grain_length: Total axial length of the propellant stack including inter-segment gaps.

action.make_neutral: Sets the segment length so the burning area stays constant through the burn (a flat pressure curve).
action.optimum_expansion: Sets the expansion ratio so the exhaust is fully expanded to the ambient pressure you entered.
action.estimate_from_altitude: Runs the 1-DOF solver and proposes three motors for your target altitude.
action.run_mission: Search for BATES motors that reach the target apogee within your constraints.
action.toggle_units: Switch every field and result between metric and imperial units.
action.apply_suggestion: Apply the suggested value and re-run the search.

warning.WARN_EXTRAPOLATED_BURN_RATE: Chamber pressure went outside the measured burn-rate table. Treat the numbers as rough; keep the pressure inside 1–11 MPa if you can.
warning.WARN_NO_EQUILIBRIUM_PRESSURE: The solver could not find a stable operating pressure. Increase the throat Ø or reduce the burning area.
warning.WARN_PRESSURE_SOLVER_FALLBACK: The pressure was found by root-finding rather than the closed form. The result is still valid; just noting the method.
warning.WARN_PROGRESSIVE_GEOMETRY: This geometry’s burn area grows during the burn, so pressure climbs. Switch to a multi-segment BATES for a flat curve.
warning.WARN_ENDBURNER_THERMAL_SOAK: An end-burner heats one spot of the case for the whole burn. Add liner thickness or keep the burn short.
warning.WARN_GRAIN_CORE_TOO_LARGE: The core is a big fraction of the outer Ø, leaving a thin web and lots of leftover sliver. Shrink the core.
warning.WARN_SLIVER_FRACTION_HIGH: A noticeable amount of propellant is left unburned at web-out. Rebalance the segment length or core Ø.
warning.WARN_FLOW_SEPARATION: The nozzle is over-expanded for this pressure and the flow will separate. Reduce the expansion ratio.
warning.WARN_UNREALISTIC_EROSION: The erosion coefficient is far higher than graphite really erodes. Lower K below 0.3 mm/s or turn erosion off.
warning.WARN_NOZZLE_OVEREXPANDED: Exit pressure is well below ambient. Reduce the expansion ratio toward the optimum shown.
warning.WARN_NOZZLE_UNDEREXPANDED: Exit pressure is well above ambient; you are leaving thrust on the table. Increase the expansion ratio.
warning.WARN_EXPANSION_RATIO_SUBOPTIMAL: The expansion ratio is far from optimal for this pressure and altitude. Use “Optimum expansion”.
warning.WARN_MEOP_EXCEEDED: Peak chamber pressure exceeds the case limit. Enlarge the throat, thicken the wall, or lower Kn.
warning.WARN_QUASI_STEADY_INVALID: The chamber fills slowly compared with the burn time, so the quasi-steady model is shaky. Use a smaller chamber or bigger throat.
warning.WARN_CONVERGENCE_NOT_REACHED: The time step did not fully converge. The totals may be off by more than 0.1 %.
warning.WARN_BURN_TIME_EXCEEDED_LIMIT: The burn ran past the simulation time limit. Check the geometry for an unrealistically thick web.
warning.WARN_EROSIVE_BURNING: Port-to-throat ratio drops below 2, so gas velocity scrubs the grain. Widen the core or the port.
warning.WARN_EROSIVE_BURNING_CRITICAL: Port-to-throat ratio drops below 1.5 — pressure is likely to spike. Widen the core significantly; the design is unsafe as-is.
warning.WARN_LSTAR_OUT_OF_RANGE: Characteristic length L* is outside the usual KNSB range. Resize the chamber free volume or the throat.
warning.WARN_LOW_FOS: Case factor of safety is below 2. Thicken the wall or lower the peak pressure before flying.
warning.WARN_MARGINAL_FOS: Case factor of safety is between 2 and 3 — acceptable but tight. Consider a thicker wall.
warning.WARN_THICK_WALL_MODEL: The wall is thick relative to the bore, so the thick-wall (Lamé) stress model is used. No action needed.
warning.WARN_BULKHEAD_FASTENERS: A lot of shear bolts are needed to hold the closures. Use a larger bolt Ø or lower the pressure.
warning.WARN_PRINT_DIRECTION_WEAK: FDM layer adhesion is weak across the print direction. Print the case hoop-wise or switch to SLS.
warning.WARN_THERMAL_LIMIT: The case inner surface is predicted to pass its service temperature. Add liner thickness or shorten the burn.
warning.WARN_NO_LINER: There is no liner. KNSB flame is ~1600 K — a plastic case needs an ablative liner. Add one.
warning.WARN_LINER_THIN: The liner is thinner than recommended for this burn time. Increase it toward the suggested value.
warning.WARN_FIT_GRAIN_DIAMETER: The grain does not fit inside the liner bore. Reduce the grain outer Ø or the liner thickness.
warning.WARN_FIT_GRAIN_LENGTH: The grain stack is longer than the space in the case. Shorten a segment, drop one, or lengthen the case.
warning.WARN_FIT_THROAT_VS_CASE: The throat Ø is larger than the case bore — geometrically impossible. Reduce the throat Ø.
warning.WARN_FIT_LINER_STACK: The liner is too thick for the case bore. Reduce the liner thickness.
warning.WARN_FIT_PORT_NONPOSITIVE: The grain has no open port. Add a core Ø.
warning.WARN_RAIL_EXIT_VELOCITY_LOW: Speed leaving the rail is below 20 m/s, so the rocket may be unstable. Use a longer rail or a punchier motor.
warning.WARN_ACCEL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: Peak acceleration exceeds your limit. Widen the throat for a softer thrust curve or raise the limit.
warning.WARN_APOGEE_UNCERTAINTY: This apogee is a 1-DOF estimate; real flights typically scatter ±15–25 %. Verify in OpenRocket.
warning.WARN_THRUST_TO_WEIGHT_LOW: Thrust-to-weight is marginal. The rocket will accelerate slowly off the rail — use a stronger motor.
warning.WARN_MISSION_INFEASIBLE: No motor in the search space met every constraint. See the binding constraint and suggested change.
warning.WARN_SOLVER_TIMEOUT: The solver hit its time budget and returned the best it found. Increase the time budget for a better search.
warning.WARN_SOLVER_BEST_EFFORT: Result is the best found within the time budget, not a proven optimum.
warning.WARN_UNCALIBRATED_DEFAULTS: You are using default c* efficiency and density factor. Enter values from a static fire for accuracy.

flight.scope: This estimate assumes vertical flight, a constant drag coefficient and still air. Real apogee typically varies by ±15–25 %. For a serious design, export the motor as .eng and verify it in OpenRocket or RockSim.
not_modelled: Stability: no CG/CP or calibre check
Cd is constant; no Mach or angle-of-attack variation
No separate fin / nose / body drag contributions

constraint.meop: Peak pressure above the case limit (MEOP)
constraint.thermal: Liner/case cannot take the thermal load

suggest.enlarge_throat_or_core: Enlarge the throat or the grain core to raise the port/throat ratio.
suggest.resize_chamber: Resize the chamber (inner Ø or length) to bring L* into range.

report.disclaimer_full: This is an engineering estimate, not a certification. Simulation results are predictions and must be verified by static fire testing. Solid propellant motors are subject to local law — do not test without proper supervision and infrastructure. NOT FLIGHT CERTIFIED — amateur research motor, simulated data only.

disclaimer.body: This is an engineering design tool, not a certification tool. Simulation results are predictions; a real motor must be verified by static fire. Solid propellant motors are subject to local law. Do not test without proper supervision and infrastructure. This application contains no information about propellant manufacture, mixing, casting or igniters.

pla.notes: Low service temperature (~45 °C). Only for very short burns and always with a generous liner.

petg.notes: Tougher than PLA with a higher service temperature; still needs a liner.

abs.notes: Higher service temperature than PETG; prone to warping when printed. Liner required.

pa12.notes: SLS nylon, nearly isotropic (factor 0.9). A good practical choice for printed cases.

pa6_cf.notes: Carbon-filled nylon: strong but layer adhesion is poor (factor ~0.45). Print orientation matters a lot.

pc.notes: Polycarbonate: high service temperature, good strength; needs a hot, enclosed printer.

al6061_t6.notes: Machined aluminium reference. Isotropic and strong; included for comparison, not 3D printed.

kraft_phenolic.notes: Kraft paper rolled with phenolic resin. The classic amateur liner; chars slowly and predictably.

cardboard.notes: Spiral-wound cardboard tube. Cheap and easy but ablates fast — use extra thickness.

graphite.notes: Graphite sleeve. Excellent thermal protection and reusable, but heavy and brittle.

ceramic_blanket.notes: Ceramic-fibre blanket. Very high temperature limit; fragile and hard to bond.

sand_epoxy.notes: Sand-filled epoxy poured in place. Good insulation, adds mass, one-shot.
